correctness.rationale: For the repaired text: mixed differences of triangular coordinates invert the upper-right rectangle sum. At index sum n−1 the relevant mixed inequality uses a zero diagonal; at sum n nonnegativity supplies the facet. The stencil's (squared norm, sum) is (4,0), (3,−1), or (1,1), so sum-zero projection and the doubled squared Frobenius length give the three stated dual norms. Ball inclusion is equivalent to all barycentric weights being at least radius times facet-normal norm; summation proves the formula and uniqueness by simultaneous equality. Counting remaining rectangles by index sum gives the Toeplitz numerator. Its quadratic part has nondecreasing increments from zero and the alpha term contributes a strictly positive superadditivity gap. The corrected face formula is the sum of nonnegative adjacent cut weights, and separates sites exactly when every cut weight is positive. D_n=n^4/12+O(n^3) and the numerator differs from d² by O(n) uniformly, yielding both limits.
residual_risks: The source reports numerical matrix-inverse and linear-program checks for n=3–10; these are not fresh results or an all-dimensional proof.
